newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AIF SAYS SYDNEY LIGHT RAIL EXTENSION OKAYED.
newsitem.headline: AIF SAYS SYDNEY LIGHT RAIL EXTENSION OKAYED.

text.p: Australian Infrastructure Fund Ltd( AIF) said on Thursday the New South Wales government approved the extensions of the Sydney Light Rail system through the city's central business district and inner west suburbs.

AIF said the extensions are the western extension to Marion Street, Leichhardt, via Glebe and Annandale in Sydney's inner west and a loop into the Central Business District via Pitt and Castlereagh Streets.
It said an Environmental Impact Study had started on the extensions. The light rail network started this week from Sydney's central station to the inner west surburb of Pyrmont.
The light rail network is operated by Sydney Light Rail Co Ltd (SLRC).
AIF, which is managed by Hastings Funds Management, has a 38.89 percent interest in the equity of SLRC, which was acquired for A$21 million on January 1, 1997.
The other major shareholders are Utilities Trust of Australia, also managed by Hastings, and Legal & General Australia, a unit of Legal & General Plc.
Sydney tore up the last of its once widespread tram track network in the early 1960s.
